content_voiceover: This slide maps out the current treatment ladder for ITP, and the headline point at the top is critical for boards, there is currently no biomarker that predicts which patient will respond to which therapy or how quickly, so treatment selection remains largely empiric and based on shared decision making. First-line therapy is corticosteroids, either prednisolone or dexamethasone, sometimes combined with IVIG for rapid platelet rise in urgent bleeding situations, but the response rate to first-line steroids is only about 20 to 30 percent durably, which is lower than many people assume and explains why so many patients progress to second-line therapy. Second-line options branch into several distinct mechanisms, TPO receptor agonists to boost production, rituximab to deplete B cells and reduce autoantibody production, fostamatinib which is a Syk inhibitor blocking the phagocytic signal in macrophages, and splenectomy which removes the primary site of antibody-mediated platelet clearance, chosen through shared decision making with the patient. For refractory ITP that fails second-line therapy, third-line strategies include splenectomy if not already done, multi-modal combination therapies combining agents with different mechanisms, and increasingly TPO-RA combined with immunomodulatory agents, alongside enrollment in investigational products and clinical trials.
keypoints: No validated biomarker predicts ITP treatment response — decision is empiric
First-line steroids/IVIG: only ~20-30% durable response rate
Second-line: TPO-RA, rituximab, fostamatinib (Syk inhibitor), splenectomy
Fostamatinib blocks Syk signaling → prevents Fc-receptor platelet phagocytosis
Refractory ITP: multi-modal combos, often TPO-RA + immunomodulatory agent
keypoint_voiceover: Key exam point, no biomarker exists to predict ITP treatment response, so this is shared decision making. First-line steroids and IVIG only give a durable response in about twenty to thirty percent of patients. Second-line brings in four different mechanisms, TPO receptor agonists, rituximab, the Syk inhibitor fostamatinib, and splenectomy. And for refractory disease, expect multi-modal combinations, often pairing a TPO-RA with an immunomodulatory agent.
